I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is medium loam, the summers are hot and dry, and the well gives me reliable water if I manage it carefully. My husband and one of my children work in town, so I manage most of the fieldwork myself, sometimes with hired day labor during cotton picking.

Cotton is my income. I plant it every year on my best 5 mu. I'll use the improved Bt variety I've been buying from the township supply cooperative — I've planted it three years running and it performs. I plough deep in spring, apply base fertilizer, then top-dress at budding and boll-setting. I irrigate about 4 times: before planting to settle moisture, at budding, at peak flowering, and once more if August is dry. Aphids and bollworm are always trouble — I spray roughly 7 times through the season. I expect around 240 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather holds.

For the 2 mu of maize — I plant it in June after the spring work on cotton is settled. I use hybrid seed, the kind sold locally. Maize doesn't need as much care. I apply urea twice and irrigate 2–3 times from the well. Two or three pesticide passes handle the corn borer and leaf diseases. I expect around 500 kg per mu.

The 1 mu of mungbean is more for the household and a little cash. I've grown the same local variety my mother grew. Mungbeans fix their own nitrogen so I go light on fertilizer. One or two irrigations, a couple of pesticide sprays. Maybe 100 kg per mu if it's a decent year.
